topic: Could the hybrid feeding structure introduce scalability challenges in dynamic payload power allocation for large-scale arrays?
consensus_response: The hybrid feeding structure can indeed introduce scalability challenges in dynamic payload power allocation for large-scale arrays. Individual amplifiers per antenna limit energy resource sharing, increasing complexity and cost. Digital beamforming (DBF) can mitigate these issues by reducing interference and increasing flexibility, but it also introduces a trade-off of increased computational resources and potential latency. Analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) can alleviate scalability challenges by reducing the number of analog amplifiers and allowing for more flexible power allocation.
